english.title: Knowingly falsify a permit - endangered species
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowingly falsified by **(..SPECIFY NATURE OF FALSIFICATION..) a permit, namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE AS IN REGULATION 2(2) OF THE CONTROL OF TRADE IN ENDANGERED SPECIES (ENFORCEMENT) REGULATIONS 1997..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 4(1) of the Control of Trade in Endangered Species (Enforcement) Regulations 1997.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)

Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence should not be used for acts carried out after 30th September 2018; the Control of Trade in Endangered Species (Enforcement) Regulations 1997 are revoked by the Control of Trade in Endangered Species Regulations 2018 (SI 2018/703) from 1st October 2018.
(ii) See also associated offence wordings H2848, H2849 and H2851 where import notification has been used for a specimen other than that which it was issued for.
(iii) See Council Regulation (EC ) No 338/97 (The Principal Regulation) and Commission Regulation (EC ) No 939/97 (The Subsidiary Regulation) for the basis of issue of the permit.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
